tasks.short: Search electronic repositories and manual sources for requested information.

steps.what: Clarify the information request and authorized search scope
Search electronic databases and repositories using keywords, metadata and document identifiers
Inspect manual catalogues or paper records absent from electronic indexes
Read candidate records and determine relevance, authority and completeness

tasks.design: Test permission-trimmed federated search in {DOCS} and the repository category of {OTHER}. Query accessible indexes once with native metadata filters, while retaining manual-archive searching and source reading; no generated answer or external disclosure is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same search must be repeated in repositories with different metadata and permissions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native connectors and federated indexes can share a query while preserving source permissions.
tasks.still_hard: Unindexed paper, poor descriptions and uncertainty about whether a source is authoritative.
tasks.human_edge: Know when a plausible hit fails to answer the actual request.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated query entry and repository navigation; source validation remains the specialist's responsibility.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: federated search can query connected repositories with permission trimming; it does not ensure source completeness or authority.

assumptions: Boundary ends with identified and read information sources. The statement does not require a report, message or record write, so none is added as a saving baseline.

Repository owners already supply document ID, title, date, type, version, location and access list. s1 produces query terms, requested dates and authorized scope. Missing metadata is searched manually; paper remains in s3.
s2 retains query refinement and inspection of native hit lists. Its reduction is repeated queries and navigation across connected repositories, not existing search computation or source reading.
Try native federation and metadata filters before custom code. If unified search already exists, its saving is zero; the estimated split is provisional.
research_questions: Does federation return all authorized test records without leaking restricted titles?

incremental.description: Check connector freshness, metadata mappings and access trimming

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 23% removes 25 repeated electronic-query hours less 2 upkeep. Low assumes fragmented or unindexable sources leave almost all searching manual. Manual archive work and reading retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Implement scanning and automated document data-entry procedures.

steps.what: Define scanning requirements, document classes and data-entry quality criteria
Configure imaging profiles, recognition rules and document-entry mappings
Test sample scans for completeness, legibility and correct document-field mapping
Approve the final capture configuration and manual exception route
Deploy the approved scanning and data-entry procedure configuration

tasks.design: Use native reusable capture profiles in the imaging-software category of {OTHER}, mapped to document fields in {DOCS}. The specialist defines class-specific rules and tests poor-quality samples before approving the exact configuration for deployment; daily scan runtime is outside this implementation saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each document class requires repeated device, recognition and mapping setup.
tasks.enabler_now: Native profile reuse can reduce repeated settings while preserving explicit exception routing.
tasks.still_hard: Unreadable pages, mixed document boundaries and false recognition of critical fields.
tasks.human_edge: Choose quality criteria and recognize that a technically successful scan lost essential meaning.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated configuration, unchanged capture-quality acceptance responsibility.

reach.task: Review capture routing and storage access

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: imaging software supports reusable capture profiles and validation rules; poor-quality documents still need explicit manual exceptions.

assumptions: This is implementing scanning procedures, not operating a scanner for every document. No scanner or recognition runtime is treated as saved human work.

s1 supplies document class, target fields, page-boundary rule, resolution, output format, required-field checks and exception destination. s2 manually maps class-specific fields; reuse covers repeated device and routing settings only.
Existing sample producers provide representative documents including low-quality and mixed-page examples. s3 retains all sample testing, comparison with originals and assessment effort.

First test native profiles and rule-based recognition in {OTHER}; no generative extraction is assumed. Missing mappings block deployment, and a changed final configuration returns to testing before approval. Shares are provisional.
research_questions: Does profile reuse preserve page boundaries and critical fields across poor-quality test documents?

already_counted.description: Final capture configuration and exception-route acceptance

incremental.description: Maintain profile compatibility and regression samples

approvals.approved_version: Exact capture configuration revision, tested mappings and exception route approved in s4; edits void deployment approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 17% removes 14 repeated-configuration and 5 deployment hours less 2 upkeep. Low assumes all class settings need manual setup, leaving only deployment. Quality criteria and tests retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze and communicate document-system performance data.

steps.what: Select and gather document-system performance logs for the reporting period
Calculate performance indicators and prepare system trend tables
Interpret performance changes and distinguish workload effects from system faults
Prepare the performance briefing with figures and explanatory conclusions
Approve the final performance briefing and authorized audience
Disseminate the approved performance briefing to internal system owners

tasks.design: Configure native performance exports from {DOCS} and the monitoring category of {OTHER}, with approved metric calculations in {BI}. Reuse figures in a {DOCS} briefing, keep interpretation and final review human, and disseminate only the approved revision to its internal audience.
tasks.previous_blocker: Periodic reports repeat exports, spreadsheet calculations and chart copying.
tasks.enabler_now: Native export schedules and metric templates can reuse a governed reporting period and definitions.
tasks.still_hard: Changing workload, caching and outages can make aggregate metrics misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Explain likely causes without mistaking correlation for a system defect.

ambition.what: Review document-search latency and ingestion failures weekly instead of only in the annual system review.

tasks.altitude: Less report assembly, more time investigating capacity and reliability trade-offs. Infrastructure change authority stays unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: operational logs and fixed formulas can generate performance trends; causal interpretation remains expert judgement.

assumptions: Boundary includes performance data gathering, analysis and internal dissemination, not remediation. Existing logging runtime is excluded; s1 shares are the human effort of selecting and gathering exports.

Existing monitoring producers supply timestamp, service ID, operation, latency, result code and queue count. Metric owner supplies period, aggregation window, exclusions and threshold; s1 confirms completeness. Missing fields require manual gathering or an explicitly incomplete report.
s3 manually produces explanatory conclusions. s4 saves only figure copying and repeated layout; explanatory writing retains time. No model attributes cause.

First test native {DOCS} and {OTHER} exports and {BI} metrics. Do not claim savings where exports or calculations already run automatically. Use aggregated system measures rather than staff performance scoring; estimates are provisional.
research_questions: Can every briefing metric be reproduced from the stated log snapshot and exclusion rules?

already_counted.description: Review final figures, conclusions and report audience

incremental.description: Maintain metric definitions and check export freshness

approvals.approved_version: Final briefing revision, source period and internal audience approved in s5; changes require reapproval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 43.4% removes 10 gathering, 30 arithmetic, 2.4 figure-copying and 3 dissemination hours less 2 upkeep. Low assumes native exports and calculations already exist, leaving dispatch only. Interpretation and final approval keep full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use native retrieval, capture and reporting features while retaining source, quality and system-meaning decisions.
role.ambitious_version: Review document-system reliability more often from reproducible metrics and verified sources.
